request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]

Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]

Admission Date: March 2017

Discharge Date: August 2018
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Initial Presentation:

The patient presented with complaints of abdominal pain for 2 months and aggravated for 1 week, leading to the diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma.

Management:

The patient was assessed by our Multi-Disciplinary Treatment (MDT) team, who recommended initiating palliative chemotherapy treatment along with apatinib. The patient tolerated the treatment well with only Grade 2 neutropenia and Grade 1 vomiting observed during treatment. Post-treatment CT scans revealed partial response with further tumor shrinkage during treatment.

Surgical Intervention:

The patient underwent total gastrectomy, D2 lymph node dissection, and Roux-en-Y anastomosis in August 2017 after being evaluated for acceptable radical surgery. The postoperative pathology report indicates no residual cancer tissue found in the resected tissue sample.

Post-Surgery Management:

After the surgical procedure, the patient recovered well and underwent maintenance treatment with apatinib in the same dose as before. No adverse events were noted in the postoperative period. However, in August 2018, the patient's ascites worsened, and adenocarcinoma cells were found by ascites biopsy, indicating disease progression.

Outcome:

The patient passed away in September 2018. The progression-free survival (PFS) period was 12 months, and the overall survival (OS) period was 17 months.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: C16

The principal diagnosis is gastric adenocarcinoma, which is a malignant neoplasm of the stomach. Category C16 covers malignant neoplasm of stomach. The episode's treatment (chemotherapy, apatinib, total gastrectomy) and the later ascites progression all relate to this condition.
